WHO.title: Who decides for the Ngäbe?
WHO.question: Four decisions about land, pensions and mining. Who made each one: the comarca, Panama's national government, or the courts?

decisions.q: Creating the Comarca Ngäbe-Buglé and holding its land in common
decisions.detail: The comarca was created by national law in 1997, after decades of Ngäbe organizing; its land is held collectively.

decisions.q: Marking the boundaries of the comarca's annex areas
decisions.detail: The 1997 law requires it, and it is still not done: in May 2026 Ngäbe leaders told a UN forum that about 150,000 people lack secure land as a result.
The National Assembly passed it in March 2025; protests in the comarca followed, and the government declared a state of emergency in neighboring Bocas del Toro.

decisions.q: Whether the Cobre Panamá mine contract stood
decisions.detail: After nationwide protests, the Supreme Court ruled the contract unconstitutional in late November 2023 and the mine stopped producing.

WHO.notice: All four were decided far from the comarca, by a government the Ngäbe vote for but do not control. The one thing the comarca holds itself, its land in common, exists because of a national law it fought for.
WHO.yourCall: If you were writing the rule for when Panama must ask the Ngäbe first, which of these four would it cover, and who would object?

decisions.q: The lowest wage a Denver employer may pay
decisions.detail: Denver sets its own minimum wage, $19.29 an hour in 2026, after Colorado let cities do so in 2019.

decisions.q: Whether Denver workers get paid family and medical leave
decisions.detail: Colorado voters approved FAMLI in 2020; it pays up to 12 weeks. A separate 2020 state law gives paid sick leave at employers of every size.
decisions.src: Denver shared mirror (FAMLI; Healthy Families and Workplaces Act)

decisions.detail: An independent 12-member commission, created when voters passed Amendment Y in 2018, took the job from the legislature.

decisions.q: Whether Denver police use license-plate cameras
decisions.detail: The city council rejected a Flock contract extension unanimously in May 2025, the mayor extended it with new limits, and in 2026 the council approved 50 Axon cameras, 7 to 6.

decisions.q: How Coloradans vote, and whether people on parole may vote
decisions.detail: Colorado mails every registered voter a ballot, registers voters automatically, and since 2019 lets people on parole vote.
decisions.src: Colorado Secretary of State; Colorado Springs Gazette

decisions.q: Whether a low-wage Denver parent can get Medicaid
decisions.detail: Colorado expanded Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act: adults qualify up to about 133% of the poverty level.
decisions.src: Denver shared mirror (Health First Colorado, HCPF)

decisions.q: Whether those Medicaid adults must report work hours from 2027
decisions.detail: The 2025 federal budget law adds work or community-engagement requirements for expansion adults from January 1, 2027, in every expansion state.

FLOOR.title: Work with no floor: Tierras Altas and Denver
FLOOR.question: Farm work in the highlands is day work, mostly without contract. What does that take away, and what does a lata of coffee pay by the hour?
FLOOR.hereLabel: Informal farm work in Tierras Altas
FLOOR.guessIntro: For each item, guess whether the work comes with it. Then check, and compare with two Denver workers: one with a payslip and one paid in cash.

rates.text: of non-farm workers in the Comarca Ngäbe-Buglé are informal; Chiriquí 52.7%; national 47.1% (Sept 2025). Farm work is not even in this count.
rates.src: INEC, Encuesta de Mercado Laboral, Sept 2025, Cuadro 7

rates.text: of Indigenous people in Panama are covered by social security (CSS), by the 2023 census as reported secondhand.

rows.q: A minimum wage that applies to you

here.text: Agriculture's minimum is $1.64 an hour at small farms, but spoken, informal farm work often sits outside it.

w2.text: $19.29 an hour in 2026, for anyone working in Denver, whatever their immigration status.

cash.text: The same law covers cash work, but 62% of 411 surveyed Denver-area day laborers had been cheated of wages.
cash.src: Galemba, University of Denver, 2016–17 (via Denver Labor)

here.text: A day you don't work is a day you aren't paid.

w2.text: 1 hour for every 30 worked, up to 48 hours a year, at every employer. It also covers a sick child and weather closures.
w2.src: CDLE, Healthy Families and Workplaces Act

cash.v: Only if the boss follows the law
cash.text: Denver Labor's 2025 cases included sick-pay violations.

rows.q: Paid time off after a new baby or a serious illness or injury

here.text: Paid leave runs through the CSS, and only for people who pay in.

w2.text: FAMLI: up to 12 weeks at about 90% of pay for lower earners, once you have $2,500 in reported Colorado wages.

cash.text: FAMLI runs on reported wages. Cash pay doesn't count.

rows.q: Pay while you look for work if the job ends

w2.text: Unemployment insurance, based on reported wages.
w2.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

cash.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

rows.q: Credit toward a pension in old age

here.text: No CSS contributions. A minimum pension of $144 is planned for people without enough of them.

w2.text: Every reported paycheck builds Social Security credits.
w2.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

cash.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

rows.q: Health care that comes with the work

here.text: Coverage through the CSS needs contributions.

w2.text: Many low-wage jobs offer none. Health First Colorado covers adults up to 133% of the poverty level whatever their job.

cash.text: The same income-based coverage is open to them.

rows.q: A pay record a bank or landlord will accept

here.text: No payslip, so no bank loan or formal lease on that income.

w2.text: A payslip and a tax record.
w2.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

cash.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

rows.q: An office that will come if you are cheated

here.text: A worker hurt the week before payday has no claim and no record of what was owed.

w2.text: Denver Labor recovered a record $2.31 million for about 7,200 workers in 2025.

cash.text: The office covers anyone working in Denver, but fewer than 40% of cheated day laborers asked for help.
cash.src: Galemba, University of Denver, 2016–17 (via Denver Labor)

grid.after: Informal doesn't mean illegal or lazy. It means work that the protections were never built to reach: social insurance, paid sick days, paid leave. Denver has informal work too. The difference is how much of all the work it is.

piece.minText: the farm minimum at small farms, $1.64 an hour
piece.intro: Coffee pickers are paid by the lata (a can of picked cherries), not by the hour. Turn the latas into an hour of work.

options.label: Coffee picked, per lata
options.text: No source publishes what a lata pays in Tierras Altas. This starts at the price that would match the farm minimum ($13.12 for an 8-hour day) at 4.5 latas a day (our arithmetic). Find the real price.
options.src: This trip’s Barriers page, Barriers 2 and 3

pace.label: Latas picked in an hour (your estimate)
pace.note: One worker reported 4–5 latas a day in Panama and 15–20 in Costa Rica, where the harvest is heavier (an anecdote, time unclear).

piece.after: Work paid by the piece is counted in pieces and prices, never in hours. The hours disappear, and so does the comparison with a wage.

den.src: CDLE, Healthy Families and Workplaces Act

month.denNote: Paid sick leave (48 hours a year) covers your own illness, a child's, and weather closures. FAMLI covers a longer illness or injury once you have $2,500 in reported wages. Both need a payslip; cash work gets neither in practice.

pay.text: The farm minimum, $1.64 an hour × 8 hours × 26 days (our arithmetic). Ngäbe workers reported farm cleaning paying about $13 a day.

month.intro: Pay comes by the day. Pick what happens this month and see who still gets paid.

events.label: Slow week: half the usual sales (3 days)
events.w2: a payslip job can cut hours too, so this is unpaid

events.label: A buyer or boss doesn't pay (1 day)
events.w2: unpaid unless a claim with Denver Labor recovers it

doing.text: Whole families travel for the harvest, often to Costa Rica for four to six months, so more hands earn.
doing.src: This trip’s Barriers page, Barriers 1 and 4

FLOOR.notice: Panama uses the dollar, so the numbers look familiar. They aren't: a full day at the farm minimum is less than one hour at Denver's minimum.
FLOOR.yourCall: What would a coffee picker need to know before the harvest to bargain for a fair price per lata? Who has that information?
